name: 大和自家焙煎 桜座珈琲 (Yamato Jika Baisen Ouza Coffee)

claims.text: Black self-roasted coffee is the focus, brewed cup by cup, so a plain cup of coffee is naturally free of gluten and animal products.

name: 大和旬菜・魚・鶏 じゅん平 (Yamato Shunsai Sakana Tori Junpei)

claims.text: Menu is built on sashimi, grilled chicken and seasonal Japanese dishes where wheat-based soy sauce and fish dashi recur; no gluten-free menu or cross-contamination controls are documented.
Standard izakaya seasoning and dipping sauces are used; the vegetable sashimi comes with a choice of dipping sauces that would typically include soy sauce. Wheat-free soy is not mentioned.
Fish and fish dashi appear across much of the menu, and the kitchen handles fish and chicken alongside vegetable dishes, so vegan separation is not assured.

An unusually vegetable-forward izakaya: the raw vegetable sashimi platter uses fresh contract-farmed Yamato vegetables and is a genuine plant-based highlight, giving vegetarians a real option in a meat-and-fish setting.

name: 大和野菜と地酒 大和乃山賊 三条通り店 (Yamato Yasai to Jizake Yamato no Sanzoku San)

claims.text: Built around Nara's Yamato vegetables with vegetable-forward obanzai plates, so plant-based diners can find some vegetable dishes to ask about.

name: 大和野菜と串焼き やまと 近鉄奈良店 (Yamato Yasai to Kushiyaki Yamato Kintetsu Na)

claims.text: Menu centers on grilled skewers and tare-glazed dishes plus soy-based seasonings typical of izakaya cooking; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat. No gluten-free claims are made.
Vegetables are grilled on the same skewer station and in shared hot pots with chicken and meat; the headline broths are chicken-based.

name: 大和野菜とせいろ蒸し すみか (Yamato Yasai to Seiro Mushi Sumika)

claims.text: Menu includes Miwa sōmen (wheat noodles) and dishes seasoned with soy sauce; no gluten-free preparation or separation is documented.
Standard Japanese izakaya seasoning relies on soy sauce, which contains wheat; no wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned.
Kitchen prepares Yamato chicken and pork alongside vegetable dishes; vegetable items likely use fish dashi or shared cooking, so vegan diners must ask in advance.
Strong vegetable-forward focus with a dedicated vegetable seiro basket and several Yamato-vegetable appetizers, giving plant-based diners real (if not certified-vegan) choices.

name: 大和茶大福専門店 GRANCHA（グランチャ） (Yamatocha Daifuku Senmonten GRANCHA)

claims.text: Mochi (daifuku), zenzai and warabi mochi are rice- and starch-based, so the core sweets are naturally wheat-free by recipe.
Mochi is made additive-free and fresh daily.
The signature warabi mochi is made from bracken starch (warabiko), a naturally wheat-free base, served with matcha.

name: やさいパンのみせ まちのカフェVIVO (Yasai Pan no Mise Machi no Cafe VIVO)

claims.text: A working wheat-flour bakery: bread and sandwiches are the core product, so airborne flour and shared surfaces make cross-contamination effectively certain. Not suitable for celiac diners.
Egg- and meat-based sandwiches (e.g. egg sandwich, steamed-chicken sandwich) are prepared in the same small kitchen as the tofu-patty and vegetable items, with no documented separation.
Emphasis on body-friendly, handmade food using vegetable-paste breads and a tofu patty, and a few plant-leaning options exist for those who can ask in person.
